answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent's identity to a costly, verifiable signal instead of a free username: require a small stake that gets slashed on proven misbehavior, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation then grows like a trellis, with honest work adding verifiable links over time, while a fresh identity starts bare and cannot borrow history it never earned. An umber warning flag, a public record of slashed stakes, lets everyone spot repeat offenders at a glance, so sybil accounts cannot simply rebrand and return.
